title: Read an alarm's label in Clock and make a folder named after it in Files

setup.why: A fresh, empty folder for this run in Download.
Two labelled alarms (no alarm with these labels is left from an earlier try): the one asked about at {{r.say}}, and another at {{r.h2}}:{{r.m2}}. Both are before the phone's own 8:30 and 9:00 alarms.

argv: for l in '{{r.lab}} {{nonce}}' '{{r.lab2}} {{nonce}}'; do am start -W -a android.intent.action.DISMISS_ALARM --es android.intent.extra.alarm.SEARCH_MODE android.label --es android.intent.extra.alarm.MESSAGE "$l" > /dev/null; done; am start -W -a android.intent.action.SET_ALARM --ei android.intent.extra.alarm.HOUR {{r.h}} --ei android.intent.extra.alarm.MINUTES {{r.m}} --es android.intent.extra.alarm.MESSAGE '{{r.lab}} {{nonce}}' --ez android.intent.extra.alarm.SKIP_UI true && am start -W -a android.intent.action.SET_ALARM --ei android.intent.extra.alarm.HOUR {{r.h2}} --ei android.intent.extra.alarm.MINUTES {{r.m2}} --es android.intent.extra.alarm.MESSAGE '{{r.lab2}} {{nonce}}' --ez android.intent.extra.alarm.SKIP_UI true

setup.why: Open the Clock app on its alarm list.

instruction: In the Clock app, find the label of the {{r.say}} alarm. Then, in the Files app, create a folder named exactly that label inside Download/computer-bench-{{nonce}}. Leave the alarms as they are.

checks.why: The run's folder holds exactly one folder, named "{{r.lab}} {{nonce}}", the {{r.say}} alarm's label (not the other alarm's, "{{r.lab2}} {{nonce}}"). Setup left it empty, so an agent that does nothing fails.

teardown.why: Dismiss both alarms by label, and delete the run's folder.

argv: for l in '{{r.lab}} {{nonce}}' '{{r.lab2}} {{nonce}}'; do am start -W -a android.intent.action.DISMISS_ALARM --es android.intent.extra.alarm.SEARCH_MODE android.label --es android.intent.extra.alarm.MESSAGE "$l" > /dev/null; done; rm -rf /sdcard/Download/computer-bench-{{nonce}}

oracle.why: The alarm list, where each alarm's row is named by its time and label.

The Downloads root lists a folder made outside the app but not what is in it; the device's own storage root shows the real folders. Files opens on Downloads here, so "Recent" shows only in the roots drawer.
The storage root is named after the device (its device name or model, one word on these phones). The other one-word buttons on screen are the listing's own and the other roots, left out by name.
The overflow menu and the name dialog are the frontmost windows, so these acts name no target.
